why: 0039, 0041 and 0042 all declared after the fact or never. This file is the declaration, and the read-back at the end of the batch is against it and against the prose, and the prose wins.

family.name: THE EIGHTH
family.one_sentence: SOMEBODY WAS TOLD A THING THEY CANNOT PLACE, AND THE CHAPTER IS A DAY ON WHICH THEY GO LOOKING FOR WHERE IT CAME FROM AND THE BOROUGH DOES NOT SUPPLY IT.
family.test_against_595_604: It cannot be summed as someone did a small thing and it went nowhere, because nothing is done. The thing in this batch is MISSING, not completed.
family.test_against_605_614: It cannot be summed as someone carried a thing they could not put down, because nothing is carried. A carried thing has weight and a place. This one has no source and no substance.
family.flag: THE FAMILY IS A WRITER'S AND NOT A HUMAN'S AND NO WRITER HAS EVER NAMED ONE BEFORE. IT IS FLAGGED, NOT DEFENDED.

declared_ordinary_word_note: Declared before chapter 0615 was written. If it comes out at nil, that is a finding about the writer and it is reported as one, which is the only correct way to report it.

bands.carried_forward_bans: A woman in her late fifties may not be used. 0600 holds two of them and the repair left it alone.
bands.note: AN ALLOCATION WHICH IS NOT READ BACK AGAINST THE PROSE IS NOT A MEASURE. IT HAS FAILED THREE TIMES. THE READ-BACK IS RUN AT THE END OF THIS BATCH AND THE PROSE WINS.

cards.0615: A woman six houses below him tells him at the bus stop that the man at the top of their road has had to go into a place. He cannot place her and cannot place where she got it. He looks for her all day. He does not go up the road.
cards.0616: A boy at the counter tells her that the flat above her has been sold. It has not been sold. She cannot work out whether he was talking about her. She spends the day establishing that he was not confusing her with somebody.
cards.0617: A face from a shop he does not use tells him over the counter that his wife has been to see somebody. He knows his wife has not been to see anybody. He cannot place the face and he does not ask his wife.
cards.0618: A customer tells him he has a daughter in her late teens. He has not got a daughter. He cannot work out whether she was talking about him, and he cannot ask her without finding out.
cards.0619: A woman she has worked beside tells her that she is the one who took it on. She cannot establish what it is and she cannot ask, because asking is the only act that would settle it.
cards.0620: A man in a car park tells him he is owed money by a firm he has never heard of. It may be real. He cannot find who told him and he does not spend it and he does not ring.
cards.0621: A stranger comes into the shop and tells her that the woman who used to work there has left and will not be back. She has never worked there. She cannot place him and cannot work out what shop he means.
cards.0622: A woman in a car park tells him that a woman he used to work with has been asking after him. He cannot establish which woman and he cannot ask without admitting he did not know.
cards.0623: A woman at a gate says that a man nobody at that gate can name has been asking after him by name. He has never given his name there. He cannot find out who knows it.
cards.0624: A woman he has met once says that he has been asking after her. He has not asked after anybody. The information turns back on him and he cannot place where it started.
